```{r panel-description, echo=FALSE}
description <- "
Panel K: AN09B017 relay subtypes differentially target mAL types
===================================================================
Panel B showed that AN09B017 variants receive a spectrum of ppk23/ppk25
input. This panel asks the complementary question: do they also show
specificity in their OUTPUT to mAL types?

Top:    Heatmap of input-normalized AN09B017 -> mAL weights (fraction of
        each mAL type's total input from each AN09B017 variant).

"
```

## Define AN09B017 subtypes

```{r an09-types}
an09_types <- c("AN09B017a", "AN09B017b", "AN09B017c", "AN09B017d",
                "AN09B017e", "AN09B017f", "AN09B017g")

# Keep only those present in the adjacency matrix
an09_in_adj <- an09_types[an09_types %in% rownames(adj.matrix)]
cat("AN09B017 subtypes in adj.matrix:", length(an09_in_adj), "/", length(an09_types), "\n")
cat(" ", paste(an09_in_adj, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# mAL types present in adj.matrix
mal_in_adj <- mal_subtypes[mal_subtypes %in% colnames(adj.matrix)]
cat("mAL types in adj.matrix:", length(mal_in_adj), "/", length(mal_subtypes), "\n")
```

## Extract input-normalized AN09B017 -> mAL connectivity

```{r an09-mal-normed}
# adj.matrix is post-normalized (input-normalized): adj.matrix[pre, post]
# Values = fraction of postsynaptic neuron's total input from presynaptic type
an09_mal_normed <- matrix(0, nrow = length(an09_in_adj), ncol = length(mal_in_adj),
                          dimnames = list(an09_in_adj, mal_in_adj))

for (a in an09_in_adj) {
  for (m in mal_in_adj) {
    an09_mal_normed[a, m] <- adj.matrix[a, m]
  }
}

cat("Input-normalized AN09B017 -> mAL matrix:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Non-zero entries: %d / %d\n",
            sum(an09_mal_normed > 0), length(an09_mal_normed)))
cat(sprintf("  Range: [%.6f, %.6f]\n", min(an09_mal_normed), max(an09_mal_normed)))

# Also extract raw synapse counts from conn
an09_mal_raw <- conn %>%
  filter(pre_type %in% an09_in_adj, post_type %in% mal_in_adj) %>%
  group_by(pre_type, post_type) %>%
  summarise(weight = sum(weight, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

cat(sprintf("  Raw connections: %d edges\n", nrow(an09_mal_raw)))
```

## Also include AN05B035 -> mAL

```{r an05b035}
# Check if AN05B035 is in the adjacency matrix
has_an05 <- "AN05B035" %in% rownames(adj.matrix)
cat("AN05B035 in adj.matrix:", has_an05, "\n")

if (has_an05) {
  an05_mal_normed <- sapply(mal_in_adj, function(m) adj.matrix["AN05B035", m])
  cat(sprintf("AN05B035 -> mAL non-zero: %d / %d\n",
              sum(an05_mal_normed > 0), length(an05_mal_normed)))

  # Combine into full relay matrix
  relay_types <- c(an09_in_adj, "AN05B035")
  relay_mal_normed <- rbind(an09_mal_normed, AN05B035 = an05_mal_normed)
} else {
  relay_types <- an09_in_adj
  relay_mal_normed <- an09_mal_normed
}
```

## Heatmap: relay -> mAL input fractions

```{r heatmap, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
# Row annotations: relay type properties
# Look up neurotransmitter from mba: consensus_nt first, then predicted_nt
relay_nt <- sapply(relay_types, function(t) {
  rows <- mba %>% filter(type == t)
  # Try consensus_nt
  nt_val <- rows %>%
    filter(!is.na(consensus_nt), consensus_nt != "") %>%
    pull(consensus_nt) %>%
    table() %>% sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>% names()
  if (length(nt_val) > 0) return(normalize_nt(nt_val[1]))
  # Fallback to predicted_nt
  if ("predicted_nt" %in% colnames(rows)) {
    nt_val <- rows %>%
      filter(!is.na(predicted_nt), predicted_nt != "") %>%
      pull(predicted_nt) %>%
      table() %>% sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>% names()
    if (length(nt_val) > 0) return(normalize_nt(nt_val[1]))
  }
  return("unknown")
})

# Get ppk23/ppk25 selectivity for AN09B017 from conn
ppk23_types <- channel_neurons[["ppk23"]]
ppk25_types <- channel_neurons[["ppk25"]]

relay_selectivity <- sapply(relay_types, function(t) {
  if (t == "AN05B035") return("sign_inverter")
  ppk23_in <- sum(conn$weight[conn$pre_type %in% ppk23_types & conn$post_type == t], na.rm = TRUE)
  ppk25_in <- sum(conn$weight[conn$pre_type %in% ppk25_types & conn$post_type == t], na.rm = TRUE)
  if (ppk23_in > ppk25_in * 1.5) return("ppk23_biased")
  if (ppk25_in > ppk23_in * 1.5) return("ppk25_biased")
  return("balanced")
})

row_annot <- data.frame(
  neurotransmitter = relay_nt,
  input_selectivity = relay_selectivity,
  row.names = relay_types
)

# Column annotations: mAL dimorphism
col_annot <- data.frame(
  dimorphism = mal_dimorphism[mal_in_adj],
  row.names = mal_in_adj
)

selectivity_colors <- c(
  "ppk23_biased"  = "#FFD92F",
  "ppk25_biased"  = "#E5C494",
  "balanced"      = "#999999",
  "sign_inverter" = "#E41A1C"
)

# Use nt_colors from setup.R, subset to values present in relay_nt
relay_nt_colors <- nt_colors[intersect(names(nt_colors), unique(relay_nt))]

ann_colors <- list(
  neurotransmitter  = relay_nt_colors,
  input_selectivity = selectivity_colors,
  dimorphism        = dimorphism_colors
)

# Diverging palette (all values are positive for input-normalized)
max_val <- max(relay_mal_normed)
if (max_val == 0) max_val <- 1
breaks <- seq(0, max_val, length.out = 101)
colors <- colorRampPalette(c("white", "#FEE5D9", "#FCAE91", "#FB6A4A",
                              "#DE2D26", "#A50F15"))(100)

save_heatmap_fixed_annot(
  mat        = relay_mal_normed,
  row_annot  = row_annot,
  col_annot  = col_annot,
  ann_colors = ann_colors,
  filename   = file.path(panel_plot_dir("panel_K_heatmap", "png"),
                         "panel_K_heatmap.png"),
  width      = 12, height = 8,
  breaks     = breaks, color = colors,
  cluster_rows = TRUE, cluster_cols = TRUE,
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  fontsize_row = 8, fontsize_col = 6,
  border_color = "grey90",
  cellwidth = 18, cellheight = 25
)

save_heatmap_fixed_annot(
  mat        = relay_mal_normed,
  row_annot  = row_annot,
  col_annot  = col_annot,
  ann_colors = ann_colors,
  filename   = file.path(panel_plot_dir("panel_K_heatmap", "pdf"),
                         "panel_K_heatmap.pdf"),
  width      = 12, height = 8,
  breaks     = breaks, color = colors,
  cluster_rows = TRUE, cluster_cols = TRUE,
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  fontsize_row = 8, fontsize_col = 6,
  border_color = "grey90",
  cellwidth = 18, cellheight = 25
)
```

## Output entropy: how broadly does each AN09B017 variant target mAL?

```{r entropy, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
# Shannon entropy of each relay neuron's output distribution across mAL types
relay_entropy <- data.frame(
  relay = relay_types,
  entropy = apply(relay_mal_normed, 1, shannon_entropy),
  n_targets = apply(relay_mal_normed > 0, 1, sum),
  total_output = rowSums(relay_mal_normed),
  selectivity = relay_selectivity,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Max possible entropy = log2(n mAL types)
max_entropy <- log2(length(mal_in_adj))
relay_entropy$normalized_entropy <- relay_entropy$entropy / max_entropy

cat("Relay output entropy:\n")
print(relay_entropy %>% arrange(entropy))

p_entropy <- ggplot(relay_entropy, aes(x = reorder(relay, entropy),
                                        y = entropy, fill = selectivity)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = max_entropy, linewidth = 0.3,
             linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = max_entropy + 0.1,
           label = "uniform", hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "grey50") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = selectivity_colors) +
  labs(x = "Relay neuron", y = "Output entropy (bits)",
       fill = "Input selectivity") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

save_fig5_plot(p_entropy, "panel_K_output_entropy", width = 8, height = 6)
print(p_entropy)
```

## Per-dimorphism-class targeting (stacked)

```{r per-class, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# For each relay neuron, sum input fractions going to male-specific vs shared mAL
dim_targeting_stacked <- data.frame()
for (r in relay_types) {
  for (dc in c("male_specific", "shared")) {
    members <- mal_in_adj[mal_dimorphism[mal_in_adj] == dc]
    if (length(members) == 0) next
    total_to_class <- sum(relay_mal_normed[r, members])
    n_in_class <- length(members)
    dim_targeting_stacked <- rbind(dim_targeting_stacked, data.frame(
      relay = r,
      dimorphism = dc,
      total_input_fraction = total_to_class,
      n_targets_in_class = sum(relay_mal_normed[r, members] > 0),
      n_in_class = n_in_class,
      mean_per_target = total_to_class / n_in_class,
      selectivity = relay_selectivity[r],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))
  }
}

# Normalized version: fraction of each relay's output going to each dimorphism class
dim_targeting_norm <- dim_targeting_stacked %>%
  group_by(relay) %>%
  mutate(fraction_of_output = total_input_fraction / sum(total_input_fraction)) %>%
  ungroup()

p_dim_norm <- ggplot(dim_targeting_norm,
                     aes(x = relay, y = fraction_of_output, fill = dimorphism)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = dimorphism_colors) +
  labs(x = "Relay neuron",
       y = "Fraction of relay output to class",
       fill = "mAL dimorphism") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

save_fig5_plot(p_dim_norm, "panel_K_dimorphism_targeting_normalized", width = 10, height = 6)
print(p_dim_norm)
```

## Per-dimorphism-class targeting

```{r per-dimorphism, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# For each relay neuron, sum input fractions going to male-specific vs shared mAL
dim_targeting <- data.frame()
for (r in relay_types) {
  for (dc in c("male_specific", "shared")) {
    members <- mal_in_adj[mal_dimorphism[mal_in_adj] == dc]
    if (length(members) == 0) next
    total_to_class <- sum(relay_mal_normed[r, members])
    dim_targeting <- rbind(dim_targeting, data.frame(
      relay = r,
      dimorphism = dc,
      total_input_fraction = total_to_class,
      n_targets = sum(relay_mal_normed[r, members] > 0),
      n_in_class = length(members),
      selectivity = relay_selectivity[r],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))
  }
}

if (nrow(dim_targeting) > 0 && length(unique(dim_targeting$dimorphism)) > 1) {
  p_dim <- ggplot(dim_targeting,
                  aes(x = relay, y = total_input_fraction, fill = dimorphism)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = dimorphism_colors) +
    labs(x = "Relay neuron",
         y = "Total input fraction to class",
         fill = "mAL dimorphism") +
    theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
      legend.position = "top"
    )

  save_fig5_plot(p_dim, "panel_K_dimorphism_targeting", width = 10, height = 6)
  print(p_dim)
}
```

## Dot plot: individual AN09B017 -> mAL connections

```{r dot-plot, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
dot_data <- as.data.frame(relay_mal_normed) %>%
  rownames_to_column("relay") %>%
  pivot_longer(-relay, names_to = "mAL_type", values_to = "input_fraction") %>%
  filter(input_fraction > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    selectivity = relay_selectivity[relay],
    dimorphism = mal_dimorphism[mAL_type]
  )

p_dot <- ggplot(dot_data, aes(x = mAL_type, y = relay)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = input_fraction, color = selectivity)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 8), name = "Input fraction") +
  scale_color_manual(values = selectivity_colors, name = "Relay selectivity") +
  labs(x = "mAL type", y = "Relay neuron") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 6),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "grey90")
  )

save_fig5_plot(p_dot, "panel_K_dot_plot", width = 14, height = 8)
print(p_dot)
```

## Panel narrative

```{r narrative, echo=FALSE}
# Summary stats
most_specific <- relay_entropy$relay[which.min(relay_entropy$entropy)]
most_broad <- relay_entropy$relay[which.max(relay_entropy$entropy)]
most_specific_targets <- relay_entropy$n_targets[which.min(relay_entropy$entropy)]
most_broad_targets <- relay_entropy$n_targets[which.max(relay_entropy$entropy)]

# Which relay targets most male_specific?
male_fracs <- dim_targeting_norm %>%
  filter(dimorphism == "male_specific") %>%
  arrange(desc(fraction_of_output))
top_male_relay <- male_fracs$relay[1]
top_male_frac <- male_fracs$fraction_of_output[1]

# Which relay targets most shared?
shared_fracs <- dim_targeting_norm %>%
  filter(dimorphism == "shared") %>%
  arrange(desc(fraction_of_output))
top_shared_relay <- shared_fracs$relay[1]
top_shared_frac <- shared_fracs$fraction_of_output[1]

n_shared_mal <- sum(mal_dimorphism[mal_in_adj] == "shared")
n_male_mal <- sum(mal_dimorphism[mal_in_adj] == "male_specific")

narrative <- sprintf(
"PANEL K: AN09B017 Output Specificity -- Relay-to-mAL Targeting
=================================================================

WHAT THIS PANEL SHOWS
---------------------
Heatmap: Input-normalized weights from each AN09B017 variant (+ AN05B035)
to each mAL type. Values represent the fraction of each mAL neuron's total
input that comes from each relay neuron. Rows clustered by output similarity;
columns clustered by input similarity and annotated by dimorphism
(male-specific vs shared).

Entropy: Shannon entropy of each relay neuron's output distribution across
mAL types. High entropy = broad targeting; low entropy = specific targeting.

Dimorphism targeting: Stacked bar chart showing what fraction of each relay
neuron's output goes to male-specific vs shared mAL types.

Dot plot: Individual connections colored by relay input selectivity.

KEY OBSERVATIONS
----------------
1. Most specific relay: %s (entropy target: %d mAL types).
   Most broad relay:    %s (%d mAL targets).

2. Dimorphism bias: %s sends %.0f%% of its output to male-specific mAL types;
   %s sends %.0f%% to shared mAL types.

3. The mAL population includes %d male-specific and %d shared types.
   Relay targeting may differ between these dimorphism classes.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
-------------------------
Panel B showed that AN09B017 variants have different ppk23/ppk25 INPUT
selectivity. This panel shows they also differ in OUTPUT specificity --
each variant preferentially innervates different subsets of mAL types.

Combined with the input selectivity spectrum, this creates a mapping:
specific pheromone channels -> specific AN09B017 variants -> specific
mAL types. The relay layer is not a simple pass-through but a
selectivity-amplifying transform that routes pheromone information to
distinct mAL subpopulations.

AN05B035 (GABAergic sign-inverter) adds a qualitatively different
output pattern: it specifically targets the mAL types that show ppk23
sign reversal (Panel C), providing the inhibitory counterweight.

PLACE IN THE FIGURE 5 STORY
----------------------------
Panel K complements Panel B by completing the relay neuron story:
- Panel B: relay INPUT selectivity (which pheromone channels drive each variant)
- Panel K: relay OUTPUT specificity (which mAL types each variant targets)

Together they show that the AN09B017 layer implements a labeled-line-like
mapping from pheromone channels to mAL subpopulations, with AN05B035
adding the sign-inverting branch.
",
most_specific, most_specific_targets,
most_broad, most_broad_targets,
top_male_relay, top_male_frac * 100,
top_shared_relay, top_shared_frac * 100,
n_male_mal, n_shared_mal
)

save_panel_narrative("panel_K", narrative)
cat(narrative)
```
